All three challenges were refuted by the evidence. H1 asked whether Construction Industries sales actually declined despite profit increasing - the evidence clearly shows sales increased 18% from $6.760 billion to $7.983 billion in Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025 (E11, E15). H2 asked whether profit margins could have increased despite declining sales - but sales did not decline, they increased 18% while profit increased 33% (E11, E13). H3 asked whether there was any disclosure showing Construction Industries sales declined - no such evidence was found; all evidence shows sales increased (E11). Note that E17 mentions expectations of "lower sales volume" in Construction Industries for Q4 2026 vs Q4 2025, but this is forward-looking and does not apply to Q3 2026 actual results.

The claim states Caterpillar posted a strong Q3 2026 "even as sales in its Construction Industries segment declined." The evidence supports that Caterpillar had a strong quarter (consolidated operating profit up 38%, operating margin up from 17.3% to 20.4%), but contradicts the assertion that Construction Industries sales declined - they actually increased 18%. This is a material factual error that contradicts the claim's premise.
